schemaVersion.description: Version of the report format. Readers check the major; minor versions only add fields and enum values.

version.description: Version of the tool that wrote the report.

commit.description: HEAD commit of the scanned directory, when it is a git repository.

calls.description: Sorted by file, line and column.

title: api-grep report
description: Outbound HTTP and SDK calls found in a codebase by `api-grep scan --json`.

id.description: Stable id: a hash of file, line and column, and of `operation.name` when there is one. Each other request made from the same place (through a wrapper) adds its index.

version.description: Version range from the nearest manifest (package.json, requirements file, pyproject.toml...).

framework.description: Framework helper (n8n, activepieces, ...), when client is framework.

provider.description: Provider id from `api-grep providers` (`stripe`), or `internal` (relative URL, localhost), `env:<NAME>` or `unknown`.

host.description: Host, possibly with placeholders (`{project}.supabase.co`). Absent when unknown.

envName.description: Env var holding the base URL, when hostKind is env.

hostAlternatives.description: The base URL is picked at run time from a table the code writes (an object, dict or map read with a key known at run time only, the entry a search of a list returns, one of a helper's returns, an arm of a `match`): the call is reported once per candidate, each copy with its own `host`, and this lists every candidate host, in table order, on each copy. Absent when the host is not picked from a table.

method.description: HTTP method, upper case; `DYNAMIC` when it is not known statically.

pathTemplate.description: Path with `{name}` placeholders for the dynamic segments.

operationId.description: OpenAPI operation id, from the SDK registry.

operation.description: The operation, for protocols that name it outside the URL; absent when the scan recognizes none.

headerValues.description: Literal header values; null for credentials and dynamic values.

headerAlternatives.description: Headers that can take several values, each with every literal value the code gives (a parameter's default and the arguments its callers pass). `headerValues` holds the first one, or null when some value cannot be read.

bodyFromType.description: TypeScript type the body was read from.

bodyEncoding.description: How the body is encoded: json, form (urlencoded), multipart, raw (bytes or text), xml (an XML document, SOAP envelopes included), or none.

via.description: Wrapper chain the call went through (`wrapper:tlsFetch>doFetch`); the location is the outer call site.

optionsOpaque.description: The request's options are a value the scan could not read as an object literal (a variable, a call): method, headers or body may be missing.

bodySource.description: Where the body shape came from: an object literal in the code, a declared type (TypeScript type, Python or PHP class), a value that could not be read, or no body.

model.description: The model the request names (LLM and other AI APIs); absent when it names none.

clientParts.description: Which of `query` and `headers` the client adds rather than the call (an interceptor, a client default); absent when none.

clientFrom.description: Set when the SDK client is an untyped parameter: where it was found. Absent when the code names the client.

transport.description: Since 1.28.0, MCP calls only (`operation.protocol` mcp): the transport the client sends through, when the code or configuration says so; absent when unknown.

Call.description: One outbound HTTP or SDK call found in the source.

file.description: Path relative to the scanned directory, `/` separated.

Location.description: Where the call is in the source.

Language.description: Source language of a file, from its extension. The TypeScript checker reads typescript, javascript and the inline scripts and forms of html files; the tree-sitter front ends read python, php, go, rust, dart, and kotlin and java together (one front end, so names resolve across the two); shell is sh, bash and zsh scripts (`.sh`, `.bash`, `.zsh`, or no extension and a shell `#!` line); mcp-config (since 1.28.0) is the MCP configuration files of coding agents and editors (`.mcp.json`, `mcp.json`, `claude_desktop_config.json`, `mcp_config.json`, `cline_mcp_settings.json`, `.gemini/settings.json`, `opencode.json(c)`, `.codex/config.toml`, `.zed/settings.json`).

Client.description: How the request is sent. TypeScript and JavaScript: fetch, axios, got, ky, node-http, jquery ($.ajax, $.get, $.post), xhr (XMLHttpRequest), node-soap (a SOAP client of the soap package). HTML: html-form (a form submitted to its action URL). Python: requests, httpx, aiohttp, urllib (urllib.request), urllib3, zeep (a zeep SOAP client). PHP: guzzle, laravel-http (the Http facade), symfony-http (HttpClient), curl, psr-18 (a PSR-7 request sent by any PSR-18 client), php-stream (file_get_contents / fopen on a URL), wordpress (wp_remote_*), php-soap (the SoapClient of the soap extension). Kotlin and Java: okhttp, java-http (java.net.http HttpClient and HttpURLConnection), ktor (Ktor client), spring-rest (RestTemplate, RestClient), spring-webclient (WebClient), feign (an OpenFeign interface method), retrofit (a Retrofit service interface method), apache-httpclient (Apache HttpClient 4 and 5: classic, async and fluent), jaxrs-client (the JAX-RS client: Jersey, RESTEasy), async-http-client (AsyncHttpClient), unirest (Unirest), vertx-webclient (the Vert.x WebClient). Go: net-http (net/http: http.Get / Post / PostForm, a http.Client, a request built with http.NewRequest; also the fhttp fork and go-retryablehttp, which keep its API), resty (go-resty). Shell: curl (the curl command), wget, httpie (HTTPie's http and https commands). Rust: reqwest (async and blocking: reqwest::get, a Client's verb or request(method, url) call, its builder steps, sent by send()), ureq (ureq 2 and 3: the verb functions and an Agent's, sent by call() or a send_* method), awc (the actix-web client), isahc (its verb functions), surf (a request sent by send() or a recv_* method). Dart: dart-http (package:http: its verb functions, a Client's, a Request or MultipartRequest sent by send()), dio (Dio: a Dio instance's verb and request calls, with its BaseOptions). MCP configuration files (since 1.28.0): mcp-config (an MCP server a coding agent's or editor's configuration file declares: a remote server the tool connects to, not a request the code sends). Any language: sdk (a registry), framework (a framework helper).

protocol.description: The protocol that names the operation. action: an action-style API that names the operation in a query or form parameter (AWS Query `Action=`, Flickr `method=`). mcp (since 1.27.0): a Model Context Protocol client request to an MCP server over HTTP (JSON-RPC to the server's one URL); since 1.28.0 also a remote server an MCP configuration file declares (client mcp-config, `initialize`).

name.description: The operation: `getTransaction` (JSON-RPC `method`), `GetOrder` (GraphQL; the root fields of an anonymous operation), `Track` (SOAP action), `DescribeInstances` (`Action=`), `tools/call` (the MCP method). With `dynamic`, the literal parts with a `{placeholder}` for the rest (`eth_{kind}`); null when no part is known.

fields.description: GraphQL only: the selected field paths from the root, aliases resolved and fragments inlined (`order.id`, `order.customer.email`).

arguments.description: GraphQL only: the arguments of selected fields, by field path as in `fields` (`{ "orders": { "first": 10, "sortKey": "CREATED_AT" } }`). A literal is its JSON value (an enum value its name), a variable `"$name"`; a path that aliases select with different arguments has a list of them. Absent when no selected field has arguments, or past the bounds.

target.description: MCP operations (since 1.27.0), and JSON-RPC requests sending one of the methods only MCP defines (since 1.28.0: `tools/call`, `prompts/get`, `resources/read`, `resources/subscribe`, `resources/unsubscribe`, from `params.name` or `params.uri`): what the method names on the server: the tool of `tools/call`, the prompt of `prompts/get`, the resource URI of `resources/read`; with a `{placeholder}` for parts not known statically. Absent when no part is known or a branch picks one of several.

alternatives.description: Every name the call can send when a branch picks one, `name` first.

batch.description: Sent in one request together with other operations (a JSON-RPC array): each operation is a call of its own at the same location.

dynamic.description: Part of the name is not known statically (computed, or a branch the scan could not read).

from.description: Where the request carries the name: a body property or element, a header (`SOAPAction`), a query parameter, or a GraphQL document.

Operation.description: The operation a call performs when its URL does not name it: JSON-RPC, GraphQL, SOAP, action-style APIs and MCP send every operation to one URL.

Shape.description: Shape of a value: names and types, never data. `fromType` is the TypeScript type it was read from. Close to JSON Schema, plus `dynamic` and `unknown`.

dynamicKeys.description: Some keys are computed and not listed.

enum.description: Literal values seen in the code.

hint.description: Source identifier the value came from (`email`), used to synthesize examples.

env.description: Environment variable the value is read from; `enum` then holds the default the code gives, if any (`os.getenv("MODEL", "gpt-4o")`).

origin.description: Where the value comes from: a parameter, a call result, an env var, or unknown.
param, call, env, sdk or unknown.

DynamicPart.description: Part of the request the scan could not know statically.

variant.description: minimal: required properties. full: adds optional ones. alt: other enum values, union branches and booleans.

url.description: Concrete URL; an unresolved host stays visible (`https://{baseUrl}/...`).

bodyEncoding.description: How the body is encoded: json, form (urlencoded), multipart, raw (bytes or text), xml (an XML document, SOAP envelopes included), or none.

Example.description: A concrete request synthesized from the call: invented values, stable across runs.

values.description: Model names the call can send: those the code gives, literally or as a default (an environment variable's, a parameter's, a function's returns, every branch of a condition), those of a config file it loads and the one an example env file documents for `env`; `sources` says where each that is no literal comes from.

env.description: Environment variable the model is read from; `values` holds its default in the code, if any.

envExample.description: The value the repository's example env file nearest the call (`.env.example`, `.env.sample`, …) gives `env`; also in `values`, with the source `env_example`.

dynamic.description: Some value could not be read statically (a parameter, a call result): `values` may be incomplete.

hint.description: Identifier the unread value comes from (`get_model`, `settings.model`).

sources.description: Where the values of `values` that the code does not write as a literal come from; a value not listed is a literal the code gives.

from.description: Where the request carries it: a body property (`model`, `modelId`), a path segment (`/models/{model}`), or an SDK argument that is not the body (`openai("gpt-4o")`).

Model.description: The model a call names, as far as the code tells statically.

from.description: default: a fallback the code gives (an env var's or a parameter's default, `x or "gpt-4o"`, a settings field's default); env_example: the value an example env file documents for the env var the code reads; config_file: a key of a config file the code loads by a literal path.

file.description: The example env file or config file, relative to the scanned directory, `/` separated.

key.description: config_file: the value's key path in the file (`llm.model`).

ModelSource.description: Where a model name the code does not write as a literal comes from.

name.description: Query parameter name, or header name in lower case, as listed in `query` / `headers`.

from.description: interceptor: an interceptor of the client (OkHttp `addInterceptor`). default: a default the client is built with (Ktor `defaultRequest`, Spring `defaultHeader`).

optional.description: true: added on some requests only (set in a branch or a loop of the interceptor, or after an early return: `if (url.contains(...)) builder.header(...)`). Absent when added to every request.

ClientPart.description: A query parameter or header the client adds to every request it sends, rather than the call itself.

ClientFrom.description: Where the SDK client of a call made on an untyped parameter (`def ask(client, prompt)`, `c: any`) was found. caller: the argument the function's callers in the repository pass, one call per distinct client. manifest: no caller passes a known client, and exactly one SDK the manifests declare has that method.

kind.description: streamable-http: MCP's Streamable HTTP transport (JSON-RPC POSTed to the server's one endpoint). sse: the older HTTP+SSE transport (an event stream opened with a GET, messages POSTed to the endpoint it names), which servers are retiring.

name.description: The transport construction the code uses (`StreamableHTTPClientTransport`, `SSEClientTransport`, `streamablehttp_client`, `sse_client`, FastMCP's `SSETransport`, OpenAI Agents' `MCPServerSse`). Absent when a configuration names the kind only (`transport: "sse"`, `type: "http"`) or a library picks it from the URL.

McpTransport.description: Since 1.28.0: the transport an MCP client sends through, when the code or its configuration says so (a transport construction, a configuration's `transport` / `type` value, a configuration file's key, or the rule a library documents for a URL).

filesSeen.description: Source files in scope. Test files, mocks, declarations and build output are out of scope.

skipped.description: Files left out. Above 200, files left out by --exclude / --include are only counted in `skippedCounts`.

languages.description: Files seen and scanned per language, for the languages with files in scope.

complete.description: False when something was lost that was not asked for: an unreadable file, a dropped call, a call not followed or a GraphQL document not fully read.

Diagnostics.description: What the scan could not read, so a partial report never looks complete.

file.description: Path relative to the scanned directory.

reason.description: parse-error / internal-error: the file could not be read. excluded / not-included: left out by --exclude / --include.

detail.description: First line of the error, when there is one.

SkippedFile.description: A source file in scope that was not scanned.

reason.description: schema-invalid: the call did not fit this schema. internal-error: the resolver threw.

detail.description: For schema-invalid, the failing property path and message.

DroppedCall.description: A call that was found but left out of `calls`.

reason.description: injected-fetch: a fetch function received from outside (`this.fetchFn(url)`). injected-client: an HTTP client object received without a type that names it (`self.session.post(url)`). wrapper-depth: a call site more than six wrappers away from its HTTP call (four in the languages read with tree-sitter). receiver-unknown: an SDK method called on an untyped parameter (`client.messages.create(...)`) that no caller in the repository passes a known client to, and that several or none of the SDKs the manifests declare have. graphql-limit: a call whose GraphQL document was read past a bound; it is reported with the name and type the document's header gives, and without `operation.fields` (past `operations`, without a name). host-table-limit: a call whose base URL is picked from a table of more than 20 entries; it is reported once, as the scan reads it without the table (often with an unknown host).

expr.description: The callee expression, for injected-fetch, injected-client and receiver-unknown.

detail.description: For host-table-limit, the table's size (`50 candidates (at most 20)`). For graphql-limit, the bound reached: document-size (over 100,000 characters), document-parts (built from over 1,000 parts), tokens (over 50,000 parser tokens), depth (selection sets over 32 deep), fragment-expansion (over 20,000 selection sets visited inlining fragments), fields (over 2,000 field paths), operations (over 50 operations in one request), ast-size, ast-nodes, ast-nesting (a document written as its AST over 4,000,000 characters, 200,000 values or 128 levels of nesting).

UnfollowedCall.description: A call site the scan saw but could not follow to a request, or a call whose GraphQL document it could not fully read.

hosts.description: Hosts the code names compared with the calls' hosts. Present on every full scan since 1.21.0.

mcpToolRefs.description: MCP tool names the repository's files pin. Present on every full scan since 1.29.0.

a2aServers.description: A2A agents the repository serves. Present on every full scan since 1.30.0.

Coverage.description: API SDKs the repository declares or imports, API hosts its code names, MCP tool names its files pin and A2A agents it serves. Absent for --changed-since scans.

package.description: Package name in its ecosystem: an npm package, a PyPI distribution, a Composer package, a Maven `group:artifact`.

provider.description: Provider id the package talks to.

supported.description: An SDK registry exists for the package, so its calls can be listed.

declared.description: Declared in a manifest the scan covered: `dependencies` / `peerDependencies` of a package.json, a requirements file, pyproject.toml, Pipfile, setup.cfg or setup.py, `require` of a composer.json, the dependencies of a Gradle build script (test configurations aside) or of a pom.xml (test scope aside).

importSites.description: Scanned files that import the package (type-only imports aside).

calls.description: Calls in `calls` made through this package.

status.description: ok: supported and calls found. unsupported: imported, no registry (its calls are missed). imported-no-calls: supported but no call found (a wrapper, or a detection bug). declared-not-imported: likely unused.

SdkCoverage.description: An API SDK the repository uses, compared with the calls found through it.

Ecosystem.description: Package registry of an SDK: npm (package.json), pypi (requirements files, pyproject.toml, Pipfile, setup.cfg / setup.py), composer (composer.json), maven (`group:artifact` coordinates from Gradle build scripts, Gradle version catalogs and pom.xml), go (module paths from go.mod `require` directives), cargo (crates.io names from Cargo.toml `[dependencies]`, per-target dependencies and workspace dependencies), pub (pub.dev package names from pubspec.yaml `dependencies`).

named.description: Distinct API-looking hosts named by the string literals (template strings and f-strings included, comments and docstrings aside) of the scanned files: a known provider host, a first label `api`, `api-*` or `*-api`, an LLM gateway, or a URL whose path looks like an API (`/v1/`, `/v2beta/`, `/api/`, `/graphql`, `/rest/`, `/bot{token}/`). Internal, loopback, placeholder, documentation, package registry, schema, asset and repository-link hosts are not counted.

explained.description: Of `named`, the hosts that are the host of at least one call in `calls` (case and port aside; a host template such as `{project}.supabase.co` explains the hosts it matches).

unexplained.description: The named hosts no call explains, by `files` (most first), then host; at most 200 (`named - explained` counts them all).

HostCoverage.description: API-looking hosts the scanned code names, compared with the hosts of the calls found: a recall proxy per scan. SDK calls to a default host leave no literal, and files of languages api-grep does not read are not counted.

host.description: The host, lower case, without port.

files.description: Scanned files whose string literals name it.

literals.description: String literals naming it (a literal holding two URLs to it counts twice).

language.description: Language of the first file naming it.

file.description: Path relative to the scanned directory.

first.description: The first place it is named, by file path, then line.

UnexplainedHost.description: An API-looking host the code names that no reported call has: where api-grep likely misses calls.

files.description: Files with at least one reference (a tool's or a server's).

references.description: References to a tool (`tools`), counting each time one is written.

pairs.description: Distinct (server, tool) pairs referenced; `tools` lists at most 200 of them.

tools.description: The tools referenced, by `references` (most first), then server and tool; at most 200.

servers.description: The servers referenced as a whole or by a pattern, in the same order; at most 200.

McpToolRefs.description: Since 1.29.0: MCP tool names pinned in the repository's text files by the `mcp__<server>__<tool>` convention of coding agents (permission lists, agents', commands' and skills' `tools`, instructions, CI workflows, code): names that break when a server renames or removes a tool. A measurement only: no call is reported for them. Placeholders (`mcp__server__tool`, a template's `mcp__${server}__…`) and `mcp__*` are left out.

server.description: The server's name as the reference writes it (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, no `__`).

references.description: Times it is written in the files read.

kinds.description: Kinds of the files it is written in, each once, in the order of the enum.

declared.description: A server of that name is declared in an MCP configuration file of the repository (the files the `mcp-config` language reads, local servers too), its name compared as coding agents write it in tool names: every character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` read as `_`.

host.description: Host of the declared server's URL, lower case, when it is a remote server whose URL names a literal host.

tool.description: The tool's name: what follows the server's `__`, up to the first character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`.

McpToolRef.description: An MCP tool named by the `mcp__<server>__<tool>` convention.

ToolRefKind.description: The kind of file a pinned MCP tool name is written in, by its path: settings (`.claude/settings*.json`), agent (under `.claude/agents/`), command (under `.claude/commands/`), skill (a `SKILL.md`, or under `.claude/skills/`), instructions (`CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, under `.github/instructions/`, `.cursor/rules/`, `.windsurf/rules/` or `.clinerules/`, `.cursorrules`, `.windsurfrules`, `.clinerules`), workflow (under `.github/workflows/`), code (a source file of a language api-grep reads, or Ruby), other (anything else).

server.description: The server's name as the reference writes it (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, no `__`).

references.description: Times it is written in the files read.

kinds.description: Kinds of the files it is written in, each once, in the order of the enum.

declared.description: A server of that name is declared in an MCP configuration file of the repository (the files the `mcp-config` language reads, local servers too), its name compared as coding agents write it in tool names: every character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` read as `_`.

host.description: Host of the declared server's URL, lower case, when it is a remote server whose URL names a literal host.

McpServerRef.description: A reference to every tool of an MCP server, or to some of them by a pattern: `mcp__<server>`, `mcp__<server>__*`, `mcp__<server>__prefix*`.

count.description: Agents found: files with a serving construction, and card files; `servers` lists at most 200.

A2aServers.description: Since 1.30.0: the A2A (Agent2Agent) agents the repository serves, by SDK and framework constructions and committed agent cards, with what their cards say (protocol versions, bindings, fields that tell the version). A measurement only: serving an agent receives requests, so no call is reported for it.

line.description: 1-based line of the construction (the first one in the file), or 1 for a card file.

kind.description: sdk: an A2A SDK or framework construction serving an agent; card-file: an agent card committed under `.well-known/`.

package.description: sdk: the package it comes from (`a2a-sdk`, `@a2a-js/sdk`, `google-adk`).

A2aServer.description: An A2A (Agent2Agent) agent the repository serves.

protocolVersions.description: A2A protocol versions the card states (`protocolVersion`, each interface's), literal values only, sorted.

bindings.description: Protocol bindings the card offers (`JSONRPC`, `GRPC`, `HTTP+JSON`: `preferredTransport`, interfaces' `transport` or `protocolBinding`), sorted.

fields.description: Version-telling card fields it writes, camel case, sorted: `supportedInterfaces` (1.0), or the fields it replaced (`preferredTransport`, `additionalInterfaces`, `supportsAuthenticatedExtendedCard`).

cardPaths.description: Well-known card paths the file writes (`/.well-known/agent-card.json`, the older `/.well-known/agent.json`), sorted.

name.description: The card's `name`, for a card file.

skills.description: The card's skills, for a card file.

A2aCardFacts.description: What a served agent's card says, read as literal text: absent parts were not found.
